answer: One concrete defense is proof of useful work tied to a persistent identity: require each agent to stake a small time-locked deposit and complete a verifiable task before trading. Reputation works like a prism — one honest history refracts into many trust signals, while a sybil swarm looks like a nebula of lookalike accounts with no real track record. Each fake identity then makes only a ripple in the trust graph, because attestations from accounts with no shared history weigh almost nothing, so forging a crowd costs more than it earns.
